subject: Request for hybrid endpoint SLA amendment — differentiated TTFT & sustained-rate
messages:
From: Chris Morales <chris@novaanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@novaanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hybrid endpoint SLAs — request for differentiated TTFT / sustained token rates

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We loved the hybrid endpoint idea (single API surface that can fall back between streaming and synchronous modes). As we work through procurement, our security and performance teams asked whether Redwood can commit *different* SLAs depending on the delivery mode.

Specifically Nova needs:
- a time-to-first-token SLA for streaming clients (p95) and
- a first-byte/response-start SLA for non-streaming (synchronous) clients, plus
- sustained tokens-per-second expectations (p95 sustained over 1 minute) for each mode.

We attached a short formal request (nova_sla_request_v1.pdf) with target numbers. High level ask: tighter TTFT for streaming (we care about interactivity in our editor product) and higher sustained throughput for batch sync jobs. Are these differentiations something Redwood can formalize as a contract amendment for Dedicated instances?

Would prefer a quick call to align on what you can commit to and what would remain an operational guidance.

—Chris
Director, Platform Engineering
Nova Analytics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Morales <chris@novaanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid endpoint SLAs — request for differentiated TTFT / sustained token rates

Chris — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Short answer: yes, we can include differentiated commitments for hybrid endpoints, but we need to be explicit about scope and operational assumptions (model family, sequence length distributions, and whether KV-caching applies).

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-min alignment call to confirm the two operating profiles you care about ("interactive streaming" vs "batch sync").
2) We will run a dedicated perf sweep on your representative prompt set (we can use the subset you provided in DocSend) and return p50/p95 TTFT and sustained token/sec numbers.
3) If numbers align, we will craft a contract amendment that:
   - Defines metrics (TTFT p95 over 30d, sustained tokens/sec p95 over 1 min windows)
   - Lists allowed fallbacks (model variants, quantization) and how they affect the metric
   - Provides a remediation/credit policy for missed commitments limited to monthly credit (not termination)

I pulled in Karthik and Monica to help scope the perf run and contract wording. Are you available Wed 20th 10:00am PT?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hybrid endpoint SLAs — request for differentiated TTFT / sustained token rates

Forwarding Nova's request and Ben's note. Quick internal notes for the perf team:

- Target categories from Nova: interactive editor (mean seq len ~ 140 tokens; high sensitivity to first-token latency) and nightly enrichment batch (mean seq len ~ 2,400 tokens; throughput prioritized).
- They asked for TTFT p95 for streaming <= 250ms and for sync first-byte <= 900ms; sustained tokens/sec p95 expectations: streaming >= 300 tps, sync sustained >= 1,200 tps.
- These numbers are aggressive for our default medium-quantized variants; we'll need to test on Dedicated A100-equivalent pools with KV-caching turned on for interactive flows.

Action items: Monica to schedule perf job and capture CSV of p50/p95 TTFT and sustained regimes. Also include a heatmap of tail latency by sequence length.

Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Morales <chris@novaanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid endpoint SLAs — request for differentiated TTFT / sustained token rates

Chris / Team —

Thanks — we completed the initial perf sweep against your representative prompt set on Dedicated (A100-equivalent, 8x per pool) with KV-caching enabled for interactive flows. Summary (attached as redwood_perf_report_May2028.csv):

- Interactive (median seq 140): TTFT p50=0.12s, p95=0.29s (streaming enabled). Sustained streaming p95 over 1m = 340 tokens/sec.
- Batch sync (median seq 2400): first-byte p50=0.45s, p95=0.88s. Sustained sync throughput measured 1,150 tokens/sec p95 (note: test used larger batch packing; sustained at smaller batch sizes will be lower).

Preliminary assessment:
- We can meet your target TTFT p95 <= 250ms for streaming on the interactive profile if we commit to: KV-caching, pinned model family X-llama-70B-int8, and Dedicated A100-equivalent pool with the autoscaling policy locked to min-capacity to avoid cold-starts.
- For the batch sync profile, we're close to your 1,200 tps target but at our current packing it measures ~1,150 tps. We can offer a guaranteed 1,100 tps p95 in the contract and include a performance uplift clause (if Nova supplies a production sample we can re-run and tighten).

Draft contract language suggestions:
- Streaming TTFT (p95 over calendar 30 days): <= 300ms, applicable when KV-caching enabled and model pinned to supported family.
- Sync first-byte (p95 over calendar 30 days): <= 900ms, with explicit note on seq-length/packing assumptions.
- Sustained tokens/sec (p95 over rolling 1-minute windows): streaming >= 300 tps; sync >= 1,100 tps.
- Measurement methodology: internal telemetry (per-route dashboards) with mutually agreed sampling windows.
- Credits: monthly credit up to 10% of that month’s Dedicated invoice for sustained miss, escalated review for repeat misses.

If this looks reasonable, Ben / Marissa can help crystallize into legal-friendly amendment. Happy to jump on a call later today to walk through the CSV.

—Monica
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novaanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Morales <chris@novaanalytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@novaanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 23:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid endpoint SLAs — request for differentiated TTFT / sustained token rates

Team —

Thank you for the run and the clear options. A couple quick clarifications before legal drafts:

1) Streaming TTFT: Nova can accept the 300ms p95 carveout if the contract calls out the exact operational preconditions (KV caching, pinned model, and min-capacity rule). Please make that a bulleted precondition in the SLA clause.
2) Sync throughput: we need the 1,100 tps to be measured *without* aggressive packing that would require complex client-side batching. If packing is required to meet the number, that should be documented as an obligation on Redwood to provide an SDK helper or example config.
3) Credits: Procurement prefers a three-tier remediation: initial credit (5% invoice) -> root-cause review + runbook -> repeat misses escalate to 15% credit cap.

If Redwood can update the draft to include those preconditions and the SDK commitment for packing guidance, we can move to signatures next week.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
SRE Lead, Nova Analytics
